title: Canadian Postal Code Meeting Point
description: Find the fair meeting centre for a set of Canadian postal codes with the Canadian Postal Code Meeting Point — each code's travel shown. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a team spread across Toronto (M), Ottawa (K) and Montreal (H) codes gets one balance point with each member's distance to it printed beside their code.
quick_answer: The Canadian Postal Code Meeting Point takes a set of Canadian postal codes, resolves each to its location, and computes the balance point — the centre that treats the set fairly — with the distance each code travels to reach it. Paste codes, one per line, and read the centre.

Serve a set of postal areas from one centre: the balance point is the first candidate, and each code's distance is the fairness audit.
Families scattered from Vancouver (V) to Halifax (B) get a centre nobody can call rigged — arithmetic is neutral in a way cousins are not.
A rep added in Calgary (T) moves the centre. Recompute after every roster change and territories stay honest.

The first letter of a Canadian code is a region: M is Toronto, K eastern Ontario, H metropolitan Montreal, V British Columbia, T Alberta. A set's letters alone sketch the map before the centre is computed.
A full code (M5V 1J1) pins a block; the FSA (M5V) pins the district. Sets mixed at FSA level still centre sensibly — precision per member varies, fairness survives.

popular_table.note: The centre is a geographic balance of the codes' locations. Roads, ferries and the St. Lawrence get their vote afterwards — the driving version is the meeting tools' road family.

faq: Full codes or just FSAs?
Both work: full codes resolve precisely, FSAs resolve to their districts. A set of either (or mixed) produces a centre; full codes make it sharpest.
Is the centre always sensible?
It is always the arithmetic balance — which can sit in a lake or a forest when codes ring one. Treat it as the fair starting point, then nudge to the nearest town.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — the codes you paste are the inputs; your own location is never asked.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Postal geography and municipal geography are different systems drawn by different bodies; a code's area and a town's boundary need not agree.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No.
Balance point or middle code?
The balance (centroid-style) point weighs every code; the middle of a road trip is a different idea — the Halfway Between Two Places tool owns that one for pairs.
US ZIP codes in the same set?
This page is Canadian-shaped. US sets belong to the Geographic Meeting Point Finder, which takes places and ZIPs.
The centre landed in a lake.
Arithmetic has no shore sense. Nudge to the nearest town on the winning shore — the distances printed tell you what the nudge costs each member.
One code is in the territories.
Northern codes stretch any centre far north. That is the fairness the set asked for; weighting by travellers per code is the organiser's amendment.
Can businesses use it for a depot?
As the first candidate, yes — then road distances, not straight lines, should referee the final site. The tool gives the geographic claim; roads audit it.
French or English place names at the centre?
Both are Canada's reality near Quebec; the centre is a coordinate, and its nearest place answers in the name the map carries.
